QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_9

question.text: For an open-ended Category III AIF, the 'High-Water Mark' (HWM) is best defined as:

answer.text: The highest GNAV ever reached gross of all fees
The highest Net Asset Value, net of operating expenses, transaction expenses and management fees, achieved by the AIF at end of year
The highest investor subscription price of any class of units
The initial subscription price at First Close

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook defines HWM as the highest NAV, net of operating expenses, transaction expenses and management fees, achieved by the AIF at year-end. If the NAV has only declined since inception, HWM equals the initial subscription price. The Trap: Option A is wrong because HWM is net of fees, not gross. Option C is unrelated. Option D applies only as the initial-price fallback when NAV has declined. Note: HWM ensures that incentive fees are paid only on genuine new performance gains above the prior peak NAV.
